heroHeadline: World's First PROTAC Drug Approved; Daraxonrasib NEJM Publication Confirms Unprecedented Survival in Pancreatic Cancer
heroSubtitle: FDA approved Veppanu (vepdegestrant) on May 1 as the first-ever PROTAC protein degrader drug for ESR1-mutant breast cancer — launching a new class of cancer therapeutics. Days later, daraxonrasib's Phase 1/2 results confirmed in NEJM (30% response rate in KRAS-mutant pancreatic cancer) ahead of full Phase 3 ASCO plenary on May 31 showing 13.2-month vs. 6.7-month OS. AI mammography triage (JACR) and Mount Sinai's quad-target combo for checkpoint-resistant colorectal cancer round out a transformative week.
footerNote: Data sourced from FDA Drug Approvals, NIH/NCI, peer-reviewed journals (NEJM, The Lancet, Nature Medicine, JACR), ASCO/ESMO/AACR conference data, and institutional analyses. All clinical data reflect published and presented trial results.
